title: Reduce streaming token latency: rewrite token loop, flush cadence, backpressure
author: Miguel Torres
description: Summary: This PR reduces streaming token generation latency by refactoring the token emission loop, changing flush cadence from fixed-interval to event-driven/adaptive flush windows, and adding backpressure signals into the scheduler. Motivation: customers observed tail latency spikes in streaming responses under bursty workloads; investigation showed buffer bloat and unnecessary flushes causing token-level jitter. This change targets runtime/token_streamer, runtime/scheduler, runtime/kv_cache interactions and kernel selection preferences to prioritize low-latency kernels for short bursts. What changed: 1) Token loop: replaced sleep/poll based loop with an event-driven loop that flushes when there is a complete token batch or when a soft flush deadline passes; 2) Flush cadence: introduced adaptive flush windows that shrink when downstream is congested and expand during steady-state to improve throughput; 3) Backpressure: scheduler now exposes a backpressure hook to token_streamer so in-flight buffers are bounded and we avoid large queue buildup; 4) KV cache alignment: aligned KV cache eviction/merge boundaries with streaming windows to reduce cache churn during flushes; 5) Kernel selection: prefer lower-latency kernels for short-sequence bursts (small token batches) and keep high-throughput kernels for large batches; 6) Observability: new token-level metrics, per-stream buffer counters, and flamegraph hooks added. Performance: in internal perf lab (A100-like cluster) we measured p50 token latency improvement of 22% (12.4ms -> 9.7ms per token) on a representative chat workload, p90 improvement 18%, and end-to-end first-token latency improvement of ~10% at the 90th percentile for 512 token sequences. CPU host overhead increased ~1% and GPU utilization became more consistent. Rollout plan: behind feature flag stream.low_latency_enabled; staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with automated regression checks. Reverts: quick rollback path implemented to revert to previous fixed-cadence flush if regressions are detected. Compatibility: no API contract changes; config knobs exposed in runtime config. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] perf harness results attached [x] docs updated [x] staged rollout plan included. Related: ENG-4231, ENG-4267.
